target: new: free part of an adnate or connate organ (length of the part above the fusion)
reason: This is a length, length (PATO_0000122), measured on a region of the bearer: the part of a filament, tepal or sepal above where it is adnate or connate. The bearer has to be that free region, so it needs a pattern rather than a quality term.
This counts stem nodes (PO_0020141) on a stem, rhizome or culm. 'With several nodes' is an indefinite count (pattern 13; a number would use pattern 03). 'At each node' is a position, not a quality.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (two annotations: bearer pubescent PATO_0000455; its trichomes PO_0000282 ferruginous = orange FLOPO:0988002)
reason: This joins two values that belong to different bearers: the part is pubescent and its hairs are rust-coloured. 'Ferruginous' already maps to FLOPO:0988002 in the colour synonyms. PATO_0070059 'rusty' is a texture (iron oxide), not this colour.
'wine', 'vinous' and 'vineux' are already RELATED synonyms of the colour class red FLOPO:0988001 in config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv, so this is the same colour.

label: glandular-striate
definition: A striated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being marked with fine lines formed by elongate glands or resin canals, usually seen as dark or translucent streaks. NOTE: The linear counterpart of FLOPO:0991174 gland-dotted (which is under PATO:0001512 punctate); common in Primulaceae-Myrsinoideae.
reason: This is a standard diagnostic character. 'Striated' alone loses the glandular nature, and gland-dotted already sets the precedent for a class.

target: new: colour of the markings (bearer spotted PATO_0000333; the spots purple PATO_0000951)
reason: A colour pattern together with the colour of its markings. Two existing values are needed, not a new term. Mapping to 'purple' alone would wrongly colour the whole part.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (part of the part: the branch of the style, stigma or inflorescence; length PATO_0000122; numbers by docs/odp/02-bounded-measurement.md)
reason: This is the length of a part of the bearer (style branches, inflorescence branches). The branch is the entity and length is the quality.
In Solanaceae 'sympodial units difoliate' means two leaves per sympodial unit, which is a count of leaves (PO_0025034) in the unit. 'leaf: difoliate' is a misattributed bearer.
Rostrate means beaked, which is FLOPO:0991028. 'Shortly' is a degree modifier and stays in the record.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (two qualities of one bearer: triangular PATO_0001875 and obtuse PATO_0001935)
reason: A compound of an outline shape and blunt angles. Both values exist, so no new term is needed.
This is a part, not a quality. 'Endosperm present' or 'very thin' are statements about PO_0009089.
Deltate maps to triangular (previous rule C226). 'Broad' is a width modifier; a ratio, when stated, belongs to pattern 11.
An indefinite count of flowers (counted part 'flowered' = flower in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv), like 'few-flowered' in pattern 13.

label: acaulescent
definition: A structural quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its having no evident above-ground stem, the leaves and inflorescences arising at or near ground level from a very short or underground stem.
reason: 'Stem absent' would be botanically false: these plants have a caudex or rhizome, which are stems. The reasoner would then flag them as contradictory, so a quality of the whole plant is needed.
The examples are lengths of drupes, pedicels, ochreae and pappus, not bristles. The label comes from a transcription error. Real bristle lengths are length on the bristle as bearer.

label: apiculate
definition: A pointed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ending abruptly in a short, sharp but flexible point. NOTE: Distinct from FLOPO:0991054 mucronate (a stiff point formed by an excurrent midrib). PATO question: PATO lists 'apiculate' as an EXACT synonym of the attribute PATO:0000944 sharpness, which is not a value.
reason: A frequent apex term with no value class. The only PATO match is an attribute. 'Shortly' stays in the record.
An inflorescence with exactly one flower is a count of flowers (PO_0009046) equal to 1.
This is a part. 'Sans ligule' and 'ligule 0' are absence statements about PO_0020105 (pattern 15). Uses on petals (corona ligules) need a check against the bearer.
The veins of the part are prominent, which follows the earlier 'veins distinct' = conspicuous rule (C176). The bearer becomes the veins of the named part.
This is a part. 'Without thorns' is absence (pattern 15). 'Thorn-tipped' is covered by FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped.
A tissue, not a quality. The statements describe its strands and layers in leaves and seed coats.

target: new: depth of a division (length of the cleft or sinus of a divided part)
reason: 'Petal clefts 0.5-1.5 mm' gives the depth of the incision of a cleft or bifid part. That is a length on a region that PO does not have, so it needs a pattern rather than a quality term.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (part of the part: the neck of the fruit, bulb or hypanthium; length PATO_0000122); necked = FLOPO:0991297
reason: This is the length of the neck of the bearer, which is a part of the part plus a measurement. Several examples ('de 2-3 x 2 mm') are mislabelled overall sizes and should be rejected one by one.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (part of the part: leaf sheath PO_0020104 increased length PATO_0000573)
reason: This says the part has a long sheath, so the length belongs to the sheath, not to the leaf or bract. Mapping it to FLOPO:0991105 sheathing alone would lose the 'long'.

label: herbaceous (sensu texture)
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being soft, green and leaf-like in substance, neither woody nor membranous nor scarious. NOTE: PATO:0002352 herbaceous is about the upper parts dying back each season, not about the texture of glumes, lemmas, phyllaries or fronds.
reason: A frequent texture term for glumes, lemmas and fronds, set against scarious and coriaceous. The PATO term with this label has a different meaning. 'Firmly' stays in the record.
Deltate maps to triangular (rule C226). 'Narrowly' is a length-to-width modifier, recorded as such or with pattern 11 when a ratio is given.

target: root (PO_0009005) present, part of stem node (PO_0020141)
reason: This states that roots arise from the stem nodes. FLOPO:0991009 creeping includes this in its definition but says more (prostrate growth), so it should not be used.
This is unequal (FLOPO:0991101) of a set of like parts or of the two sides of a leaf base. 'Very' is a degree modifier kept in the record.
'Cormous' means bearing a corm, the same model as stoloniferous (stolon present, C208).

target: new: lip of a bilabiate corolla or calyx (part of the part; length PATO_0000122); needs a FLOPO anatomy class for the lip, which PO lacks
reason: This is the length of the lower lip of a bilabiate (FLOPO:0991085) corolla, a part of the part with no PO class. The examples given are bare numbers and are not reliable.
